The new Apple Upgrade program has a key detail: "If you're leasing an iPhone, you must connect to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon at signup."

John Gruber of Daring Fireball offers a possible explanation for this requirement in a new article today.

The Apple Upgrade iPhone Restriction

According to an email shared with Gruber from a former Apple carrier team employee, the requirement primarily stems from agreements Apple reached with Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile in the United States.

The deals Apple negotiated with each carrier are worth "hundreds of millions of dollars," and in exchange for those payments, Apple made concessions. Requiring iPhones purchased through Apple Upgrade to be connected to a T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T account appears to be one of those concessions.

That former Apple employee elaborated further on the details of these agreements:

There's also a fraud and risk assessment aspect to this. A separate former Apple Store retail employee told Gruber that fraudulent iPhone sales "increased dramatically" after Apple began offering carrier financing at its retail stores.

Apple does note that while you need to connect your iPhone to AT&T, T-Mobile, or Verizon when you sign up for Apple Upgrade, the handset remains unlocked: "When leasing an iPhone, you must select a qualifying carrier (but can't use a prepaid carrier plan). The leased iPhone is always unlocked, so you can switch carriers at any time, subject to your selected carrier's terms."

You can read Gruber's full piece at Daring Fireball.
